bodies: Johns Hopkins Center for Talented Youth
Archdiocese of New York and Diocese of Brooklyn and Queens
Aspen Publishing and the University of Arizona
British Council, IDP: IELTS Australia and Cambridge University Press and Assessment
Defense Language Institute Foreign Language Center
Partnership for Assessment of Readiness for College and Careers
WIDA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison

exams.name: Character Skills Snapshot
exams.blurb: Online questionnaire that complements the SSAT by reporting a student preferences, attitudes and beliefs to independent school admission teams.

exams.name: Cognitive Abilities Test
exams.blurb: Group-administered reasoning test with verbal, quantitative and nonverbal batteries used widely for gifted and talented program screening.

exams.name: Cooperative Admissions Examination
exams.blurb: Entrance examination used by Catholic high schools in New Jersey and the Philadelphia area, covering reasoning, language and mathematics.

exams.name: High School Placement Test
exams.blurb: Catholic high school entrance and placement exam covering verbal, quantitative, reading, mathematics and language skills for eighth graders.

exams.name: Iowa Assessments
exams.blurb: Nationally normed achievement battery used by homeschool families and private schools and often paired with CogAT for gifted identification.

exams.name: ISEE Lower Level
exams.blurb: Independent School Entrance Exam level for students in grades four and five, with verbal, quantitative, reading, mathematics and an essay.

exams.name: ISEE Middle Level
exams.blurb: Independent School Entrance Exam level for students in grades six and seven applying to grades seven and eight at independent schools.

exams.name: ISEE Primary Level
exams.blurb: Shortest Independent School Entrance Exam level, given on computer to young applicants in grades two through four with a picture prompt.

exams.name: ISEE Upper Level
exams.blurb: Independent School Entrance Exam level for students in grades eight through eleven, reported in stanines with no penalty for wrong answers.

exams.name: Kaufman Brief Intelligence Test, Second Edition
exams.blurb: Brief individually administered measure of verbal and nonverbal intelligence often used to screen children for gifted programs.

exams.name: Naglieri Nonverbal Ability Test, Third Edition
exams.blurb: Language-free reasoning test using shapes and patterns, used for gifted screening of students from kindergarten through grade twelve.

exams.name: Otis-Lennon School Ability Test, Eighth Edition
exams.blurb: Group-administered school ability test measuring verbal and nonverbal reasoning, used for gifted admissions in several large districts.

exams.name: School and College Ability Test
exams.body: Johns Hopkins Center for Talented Youth
exams.blurb: Above-grade-level verbal and quantitative reasoning test used by the Center for Talented Youth to qualify students for gifted programs.

exams.name: SSAT Elementary Level
exams.blurb: Secondary School Admission Test level for students in grades three and four, with no wrong-answer penalty and an unscored writing sample.

exams.name: SSAT Middle Level
exams.blurb: Secondary School Admission Test level for students in grades five through seven, scored 440 to 710 per section with a guessing penalty.

exams.name: SSAT Upper Level
exams.blurb: Secondary School Admission Test level for grades eight through eleven, scored 500 to 800 per section and required by most boarding schools.

exams.name: Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scales, Fifth Edition
exams.blurb: Individually administered intelligence test accepted by many gifted programs and high-IQ societies for verifying cognitive ability.

exams.name: Test for Admission into Catholic High Schools
exams.body: Archdiocese of New York and Diocese of Brooklyn and Queens
exams.blurb: Entrance exam for Catholic high schools in New York City covering reading, written expression, mathematics and general reasoning ability.

exams.name: Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children, Fifth Edition
exams.blurb: Individually administered IQ test for ages six to sixteen that many private schools and gifted programs accept as cognitive evidence.

exams.name: Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence, Fourth Edition
exams.blurb: Individually administered intelligence test for children aged two through seven, commonly required for early private school admission.

exams.name: AAMC PREview Professional Readiness Exam
exams.blurb: Situational judgment test used by participating medical schools to assess how applicants respond to pre-professional competency scenarios.

exams.name: Casper Situational Judgment Test
exams.blurb: Open-response situational judgment test required by many medical, dental, nursing and health professions programs in the United States.

exams.name: Dental Admission Test
exams.blurb: Computer-based admissions test for US dental schools covering natural sciences, perceptual ability, reading comprehension and quantitative reasoning.

exams.name: Duet Values Alignment Assessment
exams.blurb: Short values-alignment assessment in the Altus Suite that compares applicant priorities with the characteristics of a specific program.

exams.name: Executive Assessment
exams.blurb: Ninety-minute business school admissions test designed for executive MBA candidates, covering integrated, verbal and quantitative reasoning.

exams.name: GMAT Focus Edition
exams.blurb: Current graduate management admissions test with Quantitative, Verbal and Data Insights sections and a total score from 205 to 805.

exams.name: GRE Biology Subject Test
exams.blurb: Graduate subject test in biology that ETS discontinued in 2021 along with the Literature in English test; it is no longer administered.

exams.name: GRE Chemistry Subject Test
exams.blurb: Graduate subject test in chemistry discontinued by ETS after the April 2023 administration and no longer available to new test takers.

exams.name: GRE General Test
exams.blurb: Graduate admissions test of just under two hours measuring verbal reasoning, quantitative reasoning and analytical writing.

exams.name: GRE Literature in English Subject Test
exams.blurb: Graduate subject test in English literature retired by ETS in 2021; English doctoral programs now rely on writing samples instead.

exams.name: GRE Mathematics Subject Test
exams.blurb: Computer-delivered subject test of about sixty-six questions on calculus, algebra and additional topics for mathematics graduate applicants.

exams.name: GRE Physics Subject Test
exams.blurb: Two-hour subject test covering classical mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics and specialised physics topics.

exams.name: GRE Psychology Subject Test
exams.blurb: Two-hour subject test of about 144 questions spanning biological, cognitive, social, developmental and clinical areas of psychology.

exams.name: JD-Next
exams.body: Aspen Publishing and the University of Arizona
exams.blurb: Eight-week online course and final assessment that law schools may use alongside or instead of the LSAT under ABA variance approval.

exams.name: Law School Admission Test
exams.blurb: Law school admissions test scored 120 to 180 that measures logical reasoning and reading comprehension plus a separate writing sample.

exams.name: Medical College Admission Test
exams.blurb: Seven-and-a-half-hour medical school admissions exam scored 472 to 528 across four sections covering sciences and critical analysis.

exams.name: Miller Analogies Test
exams.blurb: Analogy-based graduate admissions test that Pearson officially retired on 15 November 2023; score reports are no longer issued.

exams.name: Optometry Admission Test
exams.blurb: Admissions test for US optometry schools covering natural sciences, reading comprehension, physics and quantitative reasoning.

exams.name: Pharmacy College Admission Test
exams.blurb: Pharmacy school admissions test retired on 10 January 2024; PharmCAS programs no longer require or accept new PCAT scores.

exams.name: Cambridge English B2 First
exams.blurb: Upper-intermediate Cambridge English qualification at CEFR B2 level, accepted by some US institutions as evidence of English proficiency.

exams.name: Cambridge English C1 Advanced
exams.blurb: CEFR C1 Cambridge English qualification tested across reading, writing, listening and speaking and accepted by many US universities.

exams.name: Cambridge English C2 Proficiency
exams.blurb: Highest-level Cambridge English qualification at CEFR C2, demonstrating near-native mastery for academic and professional purposes.

exams.name: Duolingo English Test
exams.blurb: Adaptive online English proficiency test taken at home in about one hour and accepted by thousands of US colleges and universities.

exams.name: Examination for the Certificate of Proficiency in English
exams.blurb: Advanced English proficiency certificate at CEFR C2 issued by Michigan Language Assessment and used for academic and employment purposes.

exams.name: IELTS Academic
exams.body: British Council, IDP: IELTS Australia and Cambridge University Press and Assessment
exams.blurb: Four-skill English test scored 0 to 9 bands and required by many US universities for admission of international applicants.

exams.name: IELTS General Training
exams.body: British Council, IDP: IELTS Australia and Cambridge University Press and Assessment
exams.blurb: Version of IELTS focused on everyday and workplace English, used mainly for migration and vocational programmes rather than degree entry.

exams.name: iTEP Academic
exams.blurb: Internet-based English proficiency test reporting CEFR-aligned levels and accepted by a range of US colleges and pathway programmes.

exams.name: LanguageCert Academic
exams.blurb: Online-proctored four-skill English test designed for university admission and accepted by a growing number of US institutions.

exams.name: Michigan English Test
exams.blurb: Modular English proficiency test covering CEFR A2 to C1 that reports listening, reading, speaking and writing scores for study and work.

exams.name: PTE Academic
exams.blurb: Computer-scored English proficiency test lasting about two hours with results usually returned within two days for university admission.

exams.name: TOEFL Essentials Test
exams.blurb: Shorter adaptive ETS English test of about ninety minutes mixing academic and general tasks, accepted by a narrower set of institutions than the iBT.

exams.name: TOEFL iBT
aka: Test of English as a Foreign Language
exams.blurb: Internet-based academic English test scored 0 to 120 across reading, listening, speaking and writing and accepted by most US universities.

exams.name: TOEFL ITP
exams.blurb: Institutional paper and digital English test used internally for placement and progress monitoring rather than for university admission.

exams.name: TOEFL Junior Tests
exams.blurb: English proficiency tests for students aged eleven and older, used by secondary schools for placement and by some US boarding schools.

exams.name: TOEIC Listening and Reading Test
exams.blurb: Workplace English test scored 10 to 990 that measures listening and reading ability in everyday business and professional settings.

exams.name: TOEIC Speaking and Writing Tests
exams.blurb: Companion TOEIC assessments measuring spoken and written business English through recorded responses and written tasks.

exams.name: ACCUPLACER Advanced Algebra and Functions
exams.blurb: Computer-adaptive placement test for STEM-track students covering quadratics, functions, radicals, logarithms and trigonometry.

exams.name: ACCUPLACER Arithmetic
exams.blurb: Computer-adaptive placement test on whole numbers, fractions, decimals, percentages and comparisons of values in different formats.

exams.name: ACCUPLACER ESL Language Use
exams.blurb: Placement test for English learners measuring command of English grammar and correct sentence construction in an academic context.

exams.name: ACCUPLACER ESL Listening
exams.blurb: Placement test for English learners measuring comprehension of spoken English in lectures, conversations and everyday settings.

exams.name: ACCUPLACER ESL Reading Skills
exams.blurb: Placement test for English learners measuring comprehension of short English passages, main ideas and inference from context.

exams.name: ACCUPLACER ESL Sentence Meaning
exams.blurb: Placement test for English learners measuring understanding of vocabulary and meaning within single and paired English sentences.

exams.name: ACCUPLACER Quantitative Reasoning, Algebra, and Statistics
exams.blurb: Computer-adaptive placement test for non-STEM tracks covering rational numbers, ratios, linear equations, probability and statistics.

exams.name: ACCUPLACER Reading
exams.blurb: Computer-adaptive college placement test measuring comprehension, rhetoric, synthesis and vocabulary across single and paired passages.

exams.name: ACCUPLACER WritePlacer
exams.blurb: Essay component of ACCUPLACER scored on purpose, organisation, development, sentence variety, mechanics and critical thinking.

exams.name: ACCUPLACER WritePlacer ESL
exams.blurb: Essay component for English learners used with the ACCUPLACER ESL battery to place students into language or credit-bearing courses.

exams.name: ACCUPLACER Writing
exams.blurb: Computer-adaptive placement test on revising and editing multiparagraph text for expression of ideas and standard English conventions.

exams.name: ALEKS Placement, Preparation and Learning Assessment
exams.blurb: Adaptive mathematics placement assessment widely used by universities to place students from basic arithmetic through precalculus and calculus.

exams.name: Texas Success Initiative Assessment 2.0
exams.blurb: Statewide placement assessment required of most entering Texas public college students, covering English language arts, reading and mathematics.

exams.name: Air Force Officer Qualifying Test
exams.blurb: Multi-subtest officer selection test for the Air Force and Space Force producing composites for pilot, combat systems and academic aptitude.

exams.name: Armed Forces Qualification Test
exams.blurb: Percentile score derived from four ASVAB subtests that determines whether an applicant is eligible to enlist in a US military branch.

exams.name: Armed Services Vocational Aptitude Battery
exams.blurb: Multiple-aptitude enlistment battery used by all US military branches to determine eligibility and qualification for military occupations.

exams.name: ASVAB Career Exploration Program
exams.blurb: School-based version of the ASVAB paired with interest inventories and career planning tools for high school and postsecondary students.

exams.name: Aviation Selection Test Battery
exams.blurb: Selection battery for Navy, Marine Corps and Coast Guard aviation officer programs, including performance-based flight aptitude measures.

exams.name: Defense Language Aptitude Battery
exams.body: Defense Language Institute Foreign Language Center
exams.blurb: Aptitude test using an artificial language to predict how quickly a service member can learn a foreign language at the Defense Language Institute.

exams.name: Defense Language Proficiency Test
exams.body: Defense Language Institute Foreign Language Center
exams.blurb: Proficiency test measuring reading and listening ability in a specific foreign language for military linguists and language pay eligibility.

exams.name: Officer Aptitude Rating
exams.blurb: Three-subtest subset of the ASTB-E covering math, reading and mechanical comprehension for non-aviation Navy and Coast Guard officer programs.

exams.name: Pending Internet Computerized Adaptive Test
exams.blurb: Unproctored at-home version of the ASVAB that must be confirmed by a shortened verification test at a military entrance processing station.

exams.name: Selection Instrument for Flight Training
exams.blurb: Army aptitude test for warrant officer flight training candidates covering spatial reasoning, aviation knowledge, math and mechanics.

exams.name: Test of Basic Aviation Skills
exams.blurb: Psychomotor and multitasking test combined with AFOQT scores and flying hours to produce the Pilot Candidate Selection Method score.

exams.name: Wonderlic Cognitive Ability Test
exams.blurb: Twelve-minute fifty-question test of general cognitive ability used in employment screening and formerly at the NFL Scouting Combine.

exams.name: Wonderlic Scholastic Level Exam
exams.blurb: Short cognitive ability test used by career schools and colleges to document ability to benefit for admission and federal aid purposes.

exams.name: IB Career-related Programme
exams.blurb: IB framework for students aged sixteen to nineteen combining Diploma Programme courses with career-related study and a reflective core.

exams.name: IB Creativity, Activity, Service
exams.blurb: Mandatory ungraded Diploma Programme core component requiring a portfolio of creativity, physical activity and service experiences.

exams.name: IB Diploma Programme
exams.blurb: Two-year pre-university qualification scored out of 45 points from six subjects plus the core, widely accepted for US college credit.

exams.name: IB Extended Essay
exams.blurb: Externally assessed 4000-word independent research paper that, with Theory of Knowledge, contributes up to three bonus Diploma points.

exams.name: IB Group 1: Studies in Language and Literature
exams.blurb: Diploma Programme subject group covering Language A literature and language courses in a candidate best language at standard or higher level.

exams.name: IB Group 2: Language Acquisition
exams.blurb: Diploma Programme subject group covering Language B, ab initio and classical language courses for additional-language study.

exams.name: IB Group 3: Individuals and Societies
exams.blurb: Diploma Programme humanities group including history, economics, geography, psychology, global politics, philosophy and digital society.

exams.name: IB Group 4: Sciences
exams.blurb: Diploma Programme experimental sciences group covering biology, chemistry, physics, computer science, design technology and sport science.

exams.name: IB Group 5: Mathematics
exams.blurb: Diploma Programme mathematics group split into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at standard or higher level.

exams.name: IB Group 6: The Arts
exams.blurb: Diploma Programme arts group covering visual arts, music, theatre, film and dance, which students may replace with a second subject elsewhere.

exams.name: IB Middle Years Programme eAssessment
exams.blurb: On-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate for students in the final year of the Middle Years Programme.

exams.name: IB Theory of Knowledge
exams.blurb: Diploma Programme core course assessed by a 1600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three real-world objects.

exams.name: ACT Aspire
exams.blurb: Vertically scaled assessment system for grades three through ten that tracks growth toward ACT college readiness benchmarks.

exams.name: ACT WorkKeys Assessments
exams.blurb: Workplace skills assessments in applied math, graphic literacy and workplace documents that lead to the National Career Readiness Certificate.

exams.name: i-Ready Diagnostic
exams.blurb: Adaptive reading and mathematics diagnostic used by thousands of US districts to place students and monitor growth from kindergarten to grade twelve.

exams.name: MAP Growth
exams.blurb: Computer-adaptive interim assessment reporting RIT scores in reading, language, mathematics and science for growth tracking across grades.

exams.name: National Assessment of Educational Progress
exams.blurb: Congressionally mandated sample-based assessment that reports national and state trends in student achievement across multiple subjects.

exams.name: New York State Regents Examinations
exams.blurb: Umbrella entry for the subject-specific New York high school exit examinations in English, mathematics, science and social studies.

exams.name: PARCC Assessment
exams.body: Partnership for Assessment of Readiness for College and Careers
exams.blurb: Multi-state Common Core testing consortium wound down after 2018; its item bank now underpins successor state tests run by New Meridian.

exams.name: Smarter Balanced Summative Assessments
exams.blurb: Computer-adaptive English language arts and mathematics tests used by a multi-state consortium for grades three through eight and high school.

exams.name: Stanford Achievement Test Series, Tenth Edition
exams.blurb: Nationally normed achievement battery used by private schools and homeschool families to document reading, mathematics and content mastery.

exams.name: State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness
exams.blurb: Umbrella entry for the Texas statewide testing program covering grades three through eight plus five high school end-of-course exams.

exams.name: TerraNova, Third Edition
exams.blurb: Norm-referenced achievement test series used by private and homeschool programs to benchmark students against a national sample.

exams.name: WIDA ACCESS for ELLs
exams.body: WIDA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison
exams.blurb: Annual English language proficiency assessment used by most US states to measure listening, speaking, reading and writing growth of learners.
